questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring Scotland and a different legal system.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult due to an excessive amount of information from the universities but manageable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Almost none. Assistance in regard to register at the university and with courses wasvery difficult to get assistance with as they had not prepared for the number of students arriving.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had to find housing though AirBnb due to the housing crisis which was expensive but it was a good experience to live with locals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure to live as near as possible to the University and/or near a subway station since the buses are notoriously unreliable as they are often late.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to meet up at the University to register with my passport.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Limited avaible help due to the high number of incoming international students - I had to figure everything out on my own by asking people around and the like.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Again, due to the university's lack of preparation for the high number of students I was registered for two of my planned courses whereas the last one was decided for me by the faculty.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to be in contact with other students from your sending institution and contact the university/faculty before you leave for exchange in regard to the registration process since there are a lot of things to consider and do when you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors were competent and the courses interesting but due to the different type of legal system (common law) it was at times difficult to fully understand the legal system in Scotland as we were not offered or given any introduction/explanation to it which affected national law courses. (There were limited opportunities to select primarily international law courses due to the high number of international students and few courses). No consideration was given to international students (on exchange).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Bachelor courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Two out of three courses were primarily taught virtually and could be viewed at anytime which was very convenient as opposed to UCPH who shut down virtual teaching after COVID-19. Apart from that, the teaching style at UofG was similar to that of UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Criminal Law and Evidence
Advanced International Law 
International Private Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Criminal Law and Evidence as well a Advanced International Law as they were interesting and the knowledge I gained with these courses, I can use (to a smaller degree) in relation to my education at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UofG have over 100 different societies which included focus on different sports, nationalities, gender, sexual orientation, several types of hobbies, legal societies etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining one or more societies at the university, explore Glasgow and the highlands, the pubs etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definitely the Scottish highlands and Edinburgh. There is a Facebook group called 'International Student Tours (Scotland) Glasgow' which arranges trips to Loch Ness, Isle of Skye etc. and you see and learn a lot about Scottish culture and history - however, you only stop at beautiful view points between 10-30 min. so if you want to see these things in a a more relaxed setting you should arrange a trip yourself with some friends. 

You can visit the Isle of Arran by travelling with train from Glagow Central Station to Ardrossan Harbour and then with ferry to Brodick Station.

You can visit the Devil's Pulpit (Finnich Glen). 

And lastly, explore Glasgow which is a hidden pearl behind the "touristy" Edinburgh.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the locals were extremely friendly and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some societies and clubs at the university and go to the pubs, nightclubs etc. The local students are a bit reluctant to talk to international students but many of them are also a bit younger than e.g. Danish students as some begin studying at the university at 17. However, the more mature and older local people are generally very friendly and a heart-warming people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness, history/tradition and humour.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Involve yourself with all the possibilities that UofG has to offer, incl. events, societies etc.
2) Do not underestimate the academic level - especially if the legal system is different to yours.
3) Make sure to meet people from all over the world and go on trips during the weekends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The academic level is high - like at UCPH - so make sure to not neglect or underestimate your studies.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting wonderful people and making friends which I'm still in contact with as well as having explored Scotland and the Highlands.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) International Private Law - Was a difficut subject when you did not receive any introduction to Scottish law beforehand and no consideration was given to international students. The teacher and staff strikes during the semester also did not help and the workload and exam did not match the knowledge achieved throughout the very short semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
